Food storage and famine, yield processing, which squares can be worked, releasing a square an enemy unit occupies, unsupported units, renaming, the city actions offered and the tile and build events now call base-city-lifecycle. Every rule, id, order and number stays here, and Civilization plays the same (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008).

The wiring moves to base-goody-hut (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008): placing huts, a unit opening one, removing it, performing a random action and the two events, and the conditions of the outcomes. civ1-goody-hut keeps the rules, their order and registration, the 1-in-20 chance, the spacing of 3, the city site (Grassland, Plains or River, scoring 150 with food 8, shields 3 and trade 1, no city within 4), the barbarian distance of 4, Horseman and Swordman, and the Barbarians outcome. `unleashesBarbarians` and `BARBARIANS_FROM_CITIES` keep their signatures, every declaration file is unchanged, and so is play. core-terrain is no longer used.

The wiring moves to base-government-change (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008). civ1-government keeps the rules, their ids, order and registration, the save key `civ1-government:revolution`, Anarchy as the interim government, Despotism as the starting one, the one-to-four and two-to-eight turn durations, and the requirement entries. `lib/revolution` keeps every signature and passes the key and Anarchy to base. `Rules/AnarchyDuration` and `RevolutionError` re-export the base classes, so civ1-wonder's Pyramids rules and every `instanceof` still see one class. Play is unchanged.
refactor: a player's turns come from base-player (#13)

The research wiring moves to base-science-research (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008): each player's research and starting advances, the choose-research criteria and action, adding a city's research, working the cost out again at turn start, the started and complete events, the advance taken with a captured city, and the rule each requirement entry is played by. The civil-disorder check is base-city-happiness's inCivilDisorder and the Anarchy check base-government-change's governedBy. civ1-science keeps every rule id, the rules' order, priority and registration, the barbarian exclusions, Anarchy, ChooseResearch, the up-to-three starting advances, the cost formula and Future Technology. `requirementsRulesFor` and `deriveRequirementsRules` re-export the base functions; every other declaration is unchanged, and so is play. core-city-happiness and core-registry are no longer used.

The wiring moves to base-trade-rate (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008): civ1-trade-rate keeps the rules, their order and registration, the 50/50/0 starting rates and the round-up split, and passes them to addPlayerTradeRates, splitTrade, adjustTradeRates and processTradeRateYields. The turn-start cache stays a module-level array here, so it lives as long as it did. Every getRules signature and declaration file is unchanged, and so is play.

The remaining wiring moves to base-treasury (civ-clone/web-renderer#1008): the starting treasury (addPlayerTreasury), the overdrawn check and its event (isOverdrawn, emitTreasuryExhausted), the collection of a city's gold with the loss of an improvement its upkeep can't pay for (collectYields), and the buy-and-sell action (buyAndSell). The Anarchy check is base-government-change's governedBy. civ1-treasury keeps every rule id, the rules' order and registration, Gold and its upkeep yield, Anarchy, the Chieftain bonus and the prices. Every getRules signature and declaration file is unchanged, and so is play. core-city-happiness is only used by the tests now.
test: the conversion tests register civ1-world's TerrainChanged rules (#59)

The criteria and effects of the created, activate, validate-move, impassable, can-stow, stowed, halted, unsupported, defeated, destroyed, lost-at-sea and player action rules come from base-unit-lifecycle. The rules, their ids, order and numbers stay here, and Civ1 plays as before.

Building the world, picking a generator and picking where each player starts come from base-world-start. Civ1's numbers, the Earth map and its start positions, and the rules stay here, and Civ1 plays as before.
